newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Mar 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Mar 10.

text.p: There are 113 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that if China did not handle racial issues properly, it might follow the United States to become a target of terrorism. It said a military clampdown was just a temporary measure and Beijing must change its leftist policy towards minority groups. China should use the "one country two systems" principle to adjust its relationship with minority groups and give them real autonomy, the paper said.

-- The HONG KONG DAILY NEWS said that the increasing number of mainland immigrants had become a heavy burden on Hong Kong society. About 55,000 people moved to Hong Kong every year, causing a lot of social problems. It said that the government should talk to Beijing about reducing the number of immigrants to maintain Hong Kong's economic stability.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said that China's National People's Congress would highly appreciate the work in the past year of the Preparatory Committee laying the groundwork for Hong Kong's handover. It said the next major task of the Preparatory Committee would be to come up with detailed methods to produce the first legislative council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government.
